references.quote: In February 2021, a severe cold weather event – also known as Winter Storm Uri – caused numerous outages, derates or failures to start at electric generating plants scattered across the region. The Texas grid operator (Electric Reliability Council of Texas or ERCOT) ordered a total of 20,000 MW of rolling blackouts in an effort to prevent grid collapse; this represents the largest manually controlled load shedding event in U.S. history. More than 4.5 million people in Texas lost power – some for as long as four days. Tragically, the loss of electricity caused the deaths of numerous Texans.

outcomes.physical_supply_failure: 20,000 MW rolling blackouts in ERCOT, >4.5million people lost power; actual2021 event, not forecast
